secondaryTitle: The Unseen Hurdles of Starting Farhan Deals Online
raw:
My Farhan Deals Journey: Overcoming Online Business Startup Challenges

Today, I want to share the story behind my biggest and most recognized project: Farhan Deals. It's the name that has become my identity, a brand people remember, and my most cherished business venture.

But Farhan Deals didn't become what it is overnight. There's an interesting story behind its beginnings, filled with challenges and lessons, which I'm excited to tell you today.

My journey truly began around December 2025, though even before that, I was constantly searching for 'what to do online.' I had no idea how online business worked; frankly, it felt impossible. My father, a ranger officer, always pushed me to 'do freelancing,' 'work online,' and 'earn your own money.' On weekends, he would take me out, searching for institutes that taught online skills. We'd spend entire days looking, but never found anything. He'd get upset, asking why I didn't know where these places were, and I'd just listen, frustrated, wondering how to find something that didn't seem to exist.

Even earlier, during one of my father's holidays, we stumbled upon a place teaching Amazon e-commerce. I went with him, paid an advance of 5,000 PKR, and got admitted. The first day, they had a projector showing Amazon with some codes – I remember them typing country codes to change settings. It was all very confusing. I attended for three days, but understood nothing. It felt too advanced, and I was much younger than the other students. I told my father I couldn't grasp it. He was angry, and when he tried to get the fees back, they refused, saying we could either continue my admission or transfer it to someone else. We lost the money.

Fast forward to the last 15 days of December 2025. I was scrolling through Instagram Reels when an ad popped up: 'Learn Shopify dropshipping for free, online, with guaranteed income.' I immediately contacted them on WhatsApp. They shared a link to their WhatsApp channel, where I joined. They provided YouTube links for live classes every night from 8 to 9 PM, and if I missed a live session, the full lecture was uploaded. I'd attend live or watch the recordings, diligently completing daily homework like creating a Facebook page, connecting it to Instagram, building a portfolio, and hunting for products. The WhatsApp channel was also a community where we shared problems. For specific issues, they provided a support number. I even gave them access, and they helped set up my portfolio and ad settings. There were about 8 to 9 lectures in total; I believe they're still on a YouTube channel named Saad Bashir.

Towards the end of the course, they explained that they had taught us everything, and we could now start on our own. However, for those still confused or wanting a kickstart, they offered a full setup for 15,000 PKR. This included buying a custom domain, setting up a Shopify store, and running 2-3 testing ads – essentially a complete startup. I chose this option.

They outlined a payment plan: send 2,000 PKR after each step was completed. I sent 10,000 PKR as the work progressed. For the final 5,000 PKR, they instructed me to send 2,000 PKR to them and deposit the remaining 3,000 PKR into my bank account (Sadapay or Nayapay) to run the ads. This is where the real challenge began. I didn't have a Nayapay, Sadapay, or even a personal bank account.

After much confusion, I remembered my mother's bank account. I tried to use it, but international transactions were disabled. Despite repeated attempts to connect it, the account was permanently blocked. Now I had paid 12,000 PKR, my Shopify store with a custom domain was ready, and my social accounts were connected for ads. All that was left was to run the ads. It was January 3, 2026.

Both I and the agency were stressed. They kept pressuring me to find a bank account, giving deadlines: January 10, then January 15.

I desperately tried to open a Sadapay account using my mother's CNIC, but face verification issues kept blocking it – maybe the camera was faulty, or something else. I eventually gave up on Sadapay. Then I tried Nayapay. Verification was difficult but eventually went through. I wasn't home when Nayapay called, and my mother, confused by the questions, accidentally caused the account to be blocked. My father's account also ran into similar issues and got blocked. It felt like I was hitting a wall every time.

Finally, I gave up and told the agency, whose final 3,000 PKR I still owed, to just finish the setup; I'd manage the ads myself once I had a bank account. The truth was, I didn't have a CNIC yet, so I couldn't open my own bank account.

For a long time, I worried about the 12,000 PKR I'd spent if I couldn't run ads. Then, I remembered seeing my uncle's old checkbook at home when I was a child. I searched for it, and eventually, I found it! I discussed it with my uncle, who informed me the account hadn't been used in a long time and had been closed. I urged him to reactivate it, promising to cover all costs. We made 2-4 trips to the bank, which took about a month. They confirmed the account was active, but I needed an ATM card. Registering for an ATM card took another month. Finally, the ATM card was active, and I successfully ran ads!

Within 2-3 days, I even got 1-2 customers. The business had started! I'm still using my uncle's bank account today because I'm not yet 18. As of November 12, 2026, I am 18, and I've submitted my CNIC verification; it should be ready in a few days. After that, I'll apply for my own bank account.

This whole experience is the main reason I've kept my business somewhat limited. Even using my uncle's account has its challenges: sometimes he's at work, there are verification issues, or the balance suddenly drops to zero, blocking ads. These issues have taught me that every journey starts with difficulty, and things are rarely as easy as they seem. There are always unexpected difficulties we can't imagine beforehand.

As of November 11, my Shopify store is temporarily closed to avoid fees. Shopify charges $1 for the first three months, then around $20 (I'm not entirely sure). I've used different Gmail accounts to get the free trial multiple times. Now, I've saved a copy of my store and conduct e-commerce mainly through social accounts without a dedicated website. You can still view my Shopify store at farhandeals.store with password '1' – it's not functional for shopping, but the copy is saved, which is great.

I'm waiting for my CNIC and my own bank account to start working professionally, Inshallah. I know it won't be as simple as I imagine, but I pray it goes smoothly. Ameen.
